text_version.note: Full text of Lei 15.504/2026 (Arts. 1-5). Art. 2 restates amended provisions of Lei 11.196/2005 (Arts. 1, 2 caput, 2 §4 and new Arts. 11-A to 11-J); unchanged parts of Lei 11.196/2005 are elided ('....') on the page and not included. Provision IDs for inserted text use the article numbers of Lei 11.196/2005 (e.g. 'Lei 11.196/2005, Art. 11-B §1 I, as inserted by Art. 2').

summary.short: Amends Lei 11.196/2005 to create Redata: suspension, then zero-rating, of PIS/Pasep, Cofins, IPI and import duty on ICT equipment for accredited data-center projects in Brazil that commit to domestic-capacity, renewable-electricity, water-efficiency and R&D-investment conditions. Benefits last five years; in force 15 September 2026.
summary.long: Lei 15.504/2026 amends Lei 11.196/2005 to create Redata, a special tax regime for data-center services, and excludes data-center services from the Repes export regime. Firms implementing data-center installation, modernisation or expansion projects in Brazil may be accredited (habilitação) by the Federal Revenue Service; manufacturers supplying ICT products for an accredited firm's fixed assets may be co-accredited. Accreditation requires federal tax regularity and no Cadin record, and excludes Simples firms. Accredited firms commit to offer at least 10% of the capacity installed with Redata benefits to the domestic market (or invest an extra 10% of benefited purchases in R&D), meet sustainability criteria set by regulation, source all electricity from renewable or low-emission supply, keep water usage effectiveness at or below 0.05 L/kWh, and invest 2% of benefited purchases in R&D programmes. The domestic-capacity and R&D commitments fall by 20% in the North, Northeast and Center-West. Suspended taxes become zero-rated once commitments are met. Non-compliance leads to repayment with interest and late-payment fines, ex officio assessment, or suspension and cancellation of accreditation. Benefits last five years; PIS/Cofins/IPI benefits end 31 December 2026. The law also directs ECA Digital fines to the national children's fund for five years.

territorial_scope.description: Federal taxes on data-center projects located in Brazil; commitments reduced for establishments in the North, Northeast and Center-West regions.

entities.note: General regime; accredited firms are not named in the law (accreditation is granted case by case by the Receita Federal).

notes: Delegated to regulation or executive acts and not in this text: accreditation conditions and procedure (Art. 1 sole para., Art. 11-B caput); list of data-center services by NBS code (Art. 11-A §1); list of eligible products, Zona Franca de Manaus IPI exclusions and products without national equivalent (Art. 11-C §§4-6); sustainability criteria (Art. 11-B §1 II); free-cession multiplier, compliance terms and deadlines, exclusion procedure (§8); accreditation of independent auditors (§5); R&D programmes and private fund (§§1 V, 9). Conversion of suspended taxes into zero rate for accredited firms requires commitments II-V and incorporation into fixed assets (Art. 11-C §8); commitment I is enforced separately by suspension/cancellation (Art. 11-H). A pending Redata application does not block use of Repes (Art. 2 §4 of Lei 11.196/2005). The text does not mention Medida Provisória 1.318/2025 (br-mp1318-2025); any succession relation is not stated here. 'minors_child_safety' is coded as a domain only because Art. 3 (ECA Digital fines allocation) is an operative provision.
